In the [gist comments](https://gist.github.com/Nielk1/6d54cc2c00d2201ccb8c2720ad7538db?permalink_comment_id=3887913#gistcomment-3887913), they state:
> This logic was determined based on primarily Trial and Error. It was determined by inspecting Metro Exodus's output that only a few functions were used by the official libpad implementation. These functions utilize bit-packing to function and took some time to work out. I do not have access to libpad, so these function signatures may not match those of the official library.
> ...
> The "part of libpad" factories were found by partial reverse engineering. Some functions related to generating these values were found but were not reversed directly, instead they were monitored to determine what inputs were given to them and what outputs ended up eventually being sent to the USB device. 
> ...
> The bulk of the work was done by examining that at a specific point, the stack and CPU registers had specific values, and then shortly later the DualSense received a specific USB report structure.
> ...

The other effects were determined by intelligently fuzzing the controller after learning to avoid the debug/calibration effects and that the first byte of the effect appears safely to be the effect type enum value.
> ...
> After leaning how to reset the effect, it was reset between every random fuzz write which eliminated all false positives. Thanks to the Apple API, which appears to be a crude and direct wrapper for the official API with float parameters, testing of direct input and output was made much easier.
> ...
> Any other effect is simply leftover data and as there is no official code for them to even try to experiment with, all were invented entirely by trial and error as noted.

That being said, it may be wise for others to read through their comments more thoroughly and confirm.
